ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which tongue twister helps you practise /f/ and /v/? (1 mark)
   A. Ten tired tigers took Tom's toys.
   B. Five fat frogs fried five fine fish.
   C. Twin Tom twists ten twigs.
   D. Dina's dad did a dance.

2. Which is the best first step to look up the word 'orphan'? (1 mark)
   A. Open the dictionary at the letter o
   B. Open at the letter z
   C. Read every page
   D. Ask a friend to spell it

3. Which word means 'to make a place pretty with balloons and ribbons'? (1 mark)
   A. decorate
   B. celebrate
   C. attend
   D. graduate

4. Which word has the long vowel /ɑː/? (1 mark)
   A. market
   B. coin
   C. light
   D. burn

5. A new idea in a composition begins (1 mark)
   A. in the same sentence
   B. in a new paragraph
   C. with a question mark
   D. in capital letters

6. Which is the best way to end a story? (1 mark)
   A. With a feeling or a lesson
   B. With the word 'the'
   C. With a list of numbers
   D. With nothing

7. An inferential question needs you to (1 mark)
   A. skip the text
   B. guess without reading
   C. use clues and think
   D. copy a sentence

8. A factual question has an answer that (1 mark)
   A. is a joke
   B. you invent
   C. is stated in the text
   D. is not in the text

9. Why should there be a gap between words? (1 mark)
   A. To use more paper
   B. To make the page dirty
   C. To hide mistakes
   D. So that the words are easy to read

10. First aid words: Which word has the sound /ɒ/? (1 mark)
   A. doctor
   B. pain
   C. snake
   D. bite

11. Complete: 'That car belongs to my parents. It is ___.' (1 mark)
   A. them
   B. they
   C. theirs
   D. their

12. Which is a part of an SMS? (1 mark)
   A. The envelope
   B. The salutation address
   C. The stamp
   D. The message

13. Where do you see a reply to your email? (1 mark)
   A. In the keyboard
   B. In the outbox
   C. On the wall
   D. In the inbox

14. 'There are ___ books on the desk.' Which fits a positive statement? (1 mark)
   A. much
   B. any
   C. how
   D. some

15. Pictures and stories: Which sentence describes a feeling? (1 mark)
   A. The message travelled.
   B. She was very happy to hear from him.
   C. The computer was on.
   D. He clicked Send.

16. Which is a positive statement? (1 mark)
   A. The shed isn't locked.
   B. The shed is not locked.
   C. The shed was never locked.
   D. The shed is locked.

17. In which tense is a narrative usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Present progressive
   B. Past tense
   C. Future tense
   D. Command

18. Where does an adverb of frequency such as 'always' usually go in a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Before the main verb
   B. Inside a word
   C. Before the capital letter
   D. At the end after a full stop

19. What is the job of a comma? (1 mark)
   A. To end a sentence
   B. To show strong feeling
   C. To show a short pause and to separate items
   D. To show a question

20. Where does the comma go? (1 mark)
   A. Yes I will help,
   B. Yes, I will help.
   C. Yes I will, help.
   D. Yes I, will help.

21. What is hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Playing with friends
   B. Keeping yourself and things clean to stay healthy
   C. A school subject only
   D. A type of exercise

22. Which conjunction joins two negative ideas? (1 mark)
   A. nor
   B. and
   C. or
   D. so

23. Which paragraph plan is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Conclusion only
   B. Conclusion, details, introduction
   C. Introduction, details, conclusion
   D. Details only

24. What does a smile usually show? (1 mark)
   A. Fear
   B. Boredom
   C. Happiness or friendliness
   D. Anger

25. In which order do we read comic panels? (1 mark)
   A. Any order
   B. Bottom to top
   C. Right to left
   D. Left to right and top to bottom

26. Which is a safe habit when searching online? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing your address
   B. Clicking every pop-up
   C. Telling strangers your password
   D. Using sites your teacher approves

27. Which word begins with the cluster 'pr'? (1 mark)
   A. protect
   B. clap
   C. brush
   D. grow

28. What is the past participle of 'write'? (1 mark)
   A. written
   B. writing
   C. writed
   D. wrote

29. Which sentence is in the present perfect? (1 mark)
   A. She will finish.
   B. She finishes.
   C. She was finishing.
   D. She has finished.

30. Which preposition completes: 'The clock is ____ the door.' (higher than, not touching)? (1 mark)
   A. below
   B. above
   C. under
   D. behind

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three strategies that help you read more fluently. (3 marks)

32. Write two minimal pairs for /t/ and /d/. (2 marks)

33. Give three safety rules for using the internet. (4 marks)

34. Write four sentences using in, on, under and between. (4 marks)

35. Write a diary entry of about 60 words about a day at school. Include the date, feelings and a plan for tomorrow. (5 marks)

36. Explain how to make the sound /r/. (3 marks)

37. Write four sentences using north, south, east and west to describe the position of places near your school. (4 marks)

38. Explain the difference between a fact and an opinion, with an example of each. (3 marks)

39. Write a sentence that has an adverb of manner, an adverb of time and an adverb of place. (3 marks)

40. Complete the simile and explain it: 'as cold as ______'. (2 marks)

41. Explain the difference in meaning between 'hopping' and 'hoping'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

42. Describe three things you do before, while and after reading a story. (3 marks)

43. Make a simple plan for a story called 'The Guests Who Came Late'. (4 marks)

44. Write three sentences about a car near a bridge using one subject pronoun, one object pronoun and one possessive pronoun. (3 marks)

45. Write two similes to describe a tractor and a hot day. (2 marks)

46. Explain the proverb 'A stitch in time saves nine'. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #1 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Five fat frogs fried five fine fish.
   Five, fat, frogs, fried and fine have /f/ and five has /v/.

2. A — Open the dictionary at the letter o
   Words are in alphabetical order, so start with the first letter.

3. A — decorate
   To decorate is to make a place look pretty.

4. A — market
   Market has /ɑː/ in its first syllable.

5. B — in a new paragraph
   Each paragraph holds one idea.

6. A — With a feeling or a lesson
   A good ending gives the reader a feeling or a message.

7. C — use clues and think
   Inference means working out the answer from clues.

8. C — is stated in the text
   Factual answers can be found in the words of the passage.

9. D — So that the words are easy to read
   Gaps make the writing legible.

10. A — doctor
   Doctor has the short vowel /ɒ/.

11. C — theirs
   Theirs shows that the car belongs to them.

12. D — The message
   An SMS has a receiver, a message and a sender.

13. D — In the inbox
   Received messages are kept in the inbox.

14. D — some
   Some is used in positive statements.

15. B — She was very happy to hear from him.
   Was very happy tells a feeling.

16. D — The shed is locked.
   It has no negative word.

17. B — Past tense
   Narratives tell what happened.

18. A — Before the main verb
   For example: 'I always brush my teeth.'

19. C — To show a short pause and to separate items
   Commas mark short pauses and separate list items.

20. B — Yes, I will help.
   A comma follows 'Yes'.

21. B — Keeping yourself and things clean to stay healthy
   Hygiene protects us from germs.

22. A — nor
   'Nor' follows a negative.

23. C — Introduction, details, conclusion
   Descriptions usually run from an introduction through details to a conclusion.

24. C — Happiness or friendliness
   A smile shows a friendly feeling.

25. D — Left to right and top to bottom
   We read a comic like a book.

26. D — Using sites your teacher approves
   Approved sites and private details keep you safe.

27. A — protect
   'Protect' begins with p and r.

28. A — written
   Write, wrote, written.

29. D — She has finished.
   Has + past participle.

30. B — above
   'Above' means higher than.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Preview the text; read in phrases; follow the punctuation; re-read; read along with a model.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: ten, den and tin, din.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use it with an adult, keep your password secret, do not give your name or address to strangers, tell an adult if something frightens you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule, up to 4.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The coins are in the box. The book is on the table. The cat is under the chair. The shop is between the bank and the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: An entry in the first person with a date, events in order, feelings, a plan and a sign-off.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the date, 1 for events in order, 1 for feelings, 1 for a plan, 1 for correct tense and punctuation.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pull the tongue back a little and curl the tip up without touching the roof of the mouth, and round the lips slightly. The tongue tip touches nothing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for tongue pulled back, 1 mark for the tip not touching, 1 mark for rounded lips.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The gate is south of the classroom. The field is east of the gate. The library is west of the field. The road is north of the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: A fact can be checked, such as 'The club meets on Fridays.' An opinion is what someone thinks, such as 'Saving is a good idea.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for examples.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Yesterday the children played happily outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct adverb.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: as cold as ice, because ice is very cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable comparison and 1 mark for the explanation.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Hopping' means jumping, for example 'The rabbit is hopping.' 'Hoping' means wishing, for example 'I am hoping to win.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both sentences.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Before: read the title and predict. While: read slowly and find meanings of new words. After: answer questions and retell.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: family prepares for a party. Middle: guests do not arrive, food gets cold. Problem: they lost the way. End: they arrive, everyone laughs and eats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a beginning, 1 for events, 1 for a problem and 1 for an ending.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has bright head lights. The bridge protects us. The car is theirs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The tractor roared like a lion. The day was as hot as a burning coal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable simile.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fixing a small problem early stops it becoming a bigger problem that takes more work.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixing early and 1 for avoiding bigger work.
